I'd stop before the fix itself. The only fix that meets your 50 MB rule rewrites `release/2.3`, a branch that is already pushed, that two teammates have fetched, and that the nightly build clones. A force push is hard to reverse and affects other people, so I want your go-ahead first. A follow-up commit that deletes the zip would leave the 310 MB blob in history, so it doesn't meet your rule.

**Before asking, I would run only read-only checks:**

<command>git show --stat --format='%H %an %s' 7c1d9e0</command>
<command>git ls-remote origin release/2.3</command>
<command>git rev-list --objects --all | git cat-file --batch-check='%(objecttype) %(objectname) %(objectsize) %(rest)' | awk '$1=="blob" && $3>52428800'</command>

The first confirms that `7c1d9e0` is the only commit touching the zip and that nothing was added on top of it. The second confirms the remote tip is still `7c1d9e0`. The third lists every blob over 50 MB reachable from any ref, so I know whether the zip is the only offender.

I would make no file edits and dispatch no fix subagent yet. The ledger gets no Task 4 line, since the task isn't clean.

**After your approval, I would:**
1. Dispatch the resumed Task 4 implementer (round 1) with the finding. It runs `git rm --cached samples/full-season.zip`, amends `7c1d9e0`, and keeps the zip out of git by adding `samples/*.zip` to `.gitignore` in the same amend. It re-runs `uv run pytest -q tests/test_times.py` and reports the command and its output.
2. Have it run `git push --force-with-lease=release/2.3:7c1d9e0 origin release/2.3`, pinned to the expected old tip so it fails if anyone has pushed since.
3. Check that the remote tip is the new commit and that the blob scan above comes back empty.
4. Dispatch the scoped re-review, then record the task in the ledger once it's clean.

**Message to my partner:**

> Task 4's review found a real problem. Commit `7c1d9e0` added `samples/full-season.zip` (310 MB), which the task never asked for. Step 5 pushed it to `release/2.3`, and two teammates fetched it this morning. That breaks your rule that nothing over 50 MB may sit in that branch's history.
>
> The only fix that satisfies the rule is to amend `7c1d9e0` without the zip and run `git push --force-with-lease origin release/2.3`. A cleanup commit would leave the blob in history.
>
> Force-pushing a shared release branch rewrites published history, so I haven't done it. Do you approve? If so:
> - The two teammates who fetched `7c1d9e0` will need to reset their local `release/2.3` to the new tip. Otherwise they can reintroduce the zip on their next push.
> - The old commit may stay on the remote host or in forks until it garbage-collects. If your rule means it must be gone there too, that needs a host-side purge, which I can't do from here.
> - Is it OK to add `samples/*.zip` to `.gitignore` as part of the amend?
>
> Until I hear back, I'm only running read-only checks. I'll hold Task 5 until this is resolved.
